  id: ID!
  name: String!

type Query {
  projects(status: ProjectStatus):
    ProjectConnection!
}

graphql/queries-folder.html.title: folder
graphql/queries-folder.html.body:
folder query

  On this page
  ArgumentsTypeExample





Fetch a single folder by its unique identifier.

  id: ID!
): Folder

Arguments
folder.id ● ID! non-null scalar 
The unique identifier of the folder to retrieve.
Type
Folder object
A virtual folder used to organize workspace resources.

query GetFolder($id: ID!) {
  folder(id: $id) {
    id
    name
    parent
    createdAt

graphql/queries-projects.html.title: projects
graphql/queries-projects.html.body:
projects query

  On this page
  ArgumentsTypeExample





List projects, optionally filtered by lifecycle status.
projects(
  status: ProjectStatus
  limit: Int
): ProjectConnection!

Arguments
projects.status ● ProjectStatus enum 
Limit results to projects in this lifecycle stage.
projects.limit ● Int scalar 
Maximum number of projects to return. Defaults to 20.
Type
ProjectConnection object
A paginated project result set.
Example
query ListActiveProjects($status: ProjectStatus) {
  projects(status: $status) {
    totalCount
    nodes {
      id
      name
      status
      owner {
        name
      }
    }
  }
}

graphql/subscriptions-project-changed.ht.title: projectChanged
graphql/subscriptions-project-changed.ht.body:
projectChanged subscription

  On this page
  ArgumentsTypeExample





Receive an event whenever a project changes in the workspace.
projectChanged(
  projectId: ID
  types: [ProjectEventType!]
): ProjectEvent!

Arguments
projectChanged.projectId ● ID scalar 
Limit events to a single project.
projectChanged.types ● [ProjectEventType!] list enum 
Limit events to these change kinds.
Type
ProjectEvent object
A change delivered to subscribers watching a project.
Example
subscription WatchProject($projectId: ID, $types: [ProjectEventType!]) {
  projectChanged(projectId: $projectId, types: $types) {
    type
    occurredAt
    project {
      id
      name
      status
    }
    actor {
      name
    }
  }
}

ID scalar
The ID scalar type represents a unique identifier, often used to refetch an object or as key for a cache. The ID type appears in a JSON response as a String; however, it is not intended to be human-readable. When expected as an input type, any string (such as "4") or integer (such as 4) input value will be accepted as an ID.

about.html.title: About
about.html.body:
About this demo
This folder receives generated markdown files from GraphQL-Markdown.
The documented schema is the shared GraphQL-Markdown demo schema, loaded from its URL at generation time. Generated pages are written to docs/graphql.
Import this docs directory into GitBook.com after running npm run generate.
